implement.approach: Test-first: committed the seeded-PII native envelope regression before any implementation (fails on base: module missing and cocoa events rejected). Minimal general fix inside write_paths: a single scrub module with a shared deny-list applied both as a redactor for native free text and as a final gate over every finished event (JS and native), plus allow-list reconstruction for cocoa crashes; wired into the three shipping entry points in sentry.ts (beforeSend, transport, handled-error reporter) without changing any gating/disable flags.
baseline_failures_observed: None inside src/diagnostics. Full mobile suite on HEAD (`cd apps/mobile && npx jest --ci --silent`): 308 suites passed, 1 suite skipped (pre-existing skip, outside write_paths, unchanged), 5916 passed / 1 skipped — artifacts/w10-01/full-mobile-jest.log
residual_risks: The native allow-list was validated against a hand-built cocoa fixture shaped after the Sentry Cocoa event schema (INFERRED from SDK typings/docs), not against an envelope captured from a real iOS crash — real-device verification of the native envelope shape remains Mac-plane work and diagnostics stay disabled until that gate is approved.

Deny-list regexes are heuristic: free-text scrubbing is deliberately aggressive (any slash-rooted token, UUIDs, 32+ hex runs, base64-like blobs, phone-like digit groups are redacted), which may over-redact legitimate C++/Swift symbols containing '/'; under-detection remains possible for novel identifier formats, so the field allow-list (not the deny-list) is the primary control.

Sentry Cocoa's own native SDK scrubbing (beforeSend on the native side) is not available from JS; this scrubber runs on envelopes that reach the JS transport, so native envelopes cached and sent directly by the native SDK would bypass it — a reason enableNative/autoInitializeNativeSdk/enableNativeCrashHandling must remain false (they do).
implement.summary: Gap on BASE_SHA (INFERRED from code, VERIFIED by the base run): apps/mobile/src/diagnostics/privacy.ts minimizeDiagnosticEvent (the `platform !== 'javascript'` guard, ~line 258 of base) rejects every non-JS event, so a native/cocoa crash envelope is dropped, never scrubbed; minimizeDiagnosticEnvelope and createFilteredTransport only route JS events; sentry.ts beforeSend/transport/createErrorReporter call only minimizeDiagnosticEvent; there is no deny-list at all — a JS event that passed the field allow-list could still carry a path/email/token inside an allowed string, and no scrub.ts existed. Fix (commits 59fbff5a test, 94b7dd30 test fixture tightening, e5cda153 impl, f57804e7 impl follow-up): new apps/mobile/src/diagnostics/scrub.ts provides (a) GATE_RULES/TEXT_RULES deny-list (filesystem paths incl. ~/, ./, file:, Windows; emails; bearer/basic tokens, JWTs, `token=`/`secret=`-style query secrets, vendor key prefixes; media schemes ph://, assets-library://, content://, blob://, photo-library `UUID/L0/nnn` ids, data: URIs, media file names; IPv4/IPv6/MAC; and for free text also UUIDs, 32+ hex, base64-like blobs, phone numbers) exposed as scrubDiagnosticText (redaction, bounded 1024 chars, fixed-point ≤8 passes) and findDeniedDiagnosticContent (recursive walk of every string and key with cycle/size guards, fail-closed 'unreadable'); (b) minimizeNativeDiagnosticEvent: allow-list reconstruction of a cocoa error/fatal event — validated release identity, event_id/timestamp (number or ISO), sdk name from a fixed set + semver, categorical app/device/os fields only (no names, ids, timezone, locale, boot time), exceptions bounded to 3 with native mechanism types mach/signal/nsexception/cpp_exception, numeric signal/mach meta, frames bounded to the last 50 requiring a hex instruction_addr and keeping only scrubbed function symbol, package basename, symbol/image addresses, in_app; Mach-O debug images bounded to 50, lowercase debug_id, kept only when referenced by a frame; everything else (user, request, breadcrumbs, extra, threads, message, fingerprint, modules, unknown keys) dropped; (c) scrubDiagnosticEvent dispatching cocoa→native, javascript→existing minimizeDiagnosticEvent, everything else→null, then gating the finished event through the deny-list; (d) scrubDiagnosticEnvelope/createScrubbedTransport rebuilding the envelope with only the single sanitized event item (attachments/sessions dropped) and failing closed to {} on error. privacy.ts change is additive only (`export` on record/boundedItems). sentry.ts wiring: beforeSend, the transport wrapper and createErrorReporter now go through scrubDiagnosticEvent/createScrubbedTransport; every native collection flag stays false, transport stays disabled by default (runtimeConfig unchanged, `enabled` still requires a DSN), NATIVE_DIAGNOSTICS_STATUS unchanged, no comments modified. Regression test apps/mobile/src/diagnostics/__tests__/scrub.test.ts (27 tests) seeds SENSITIVE_FIXTURE_DO_NOT_TRANSMIT, an install UUID, email, JWT, file:// media URI, ph:// photo id, IPv4 and device name into a cocoa crash envelope and asserts the scrubbed output equals the exact allow-listed shape with none of the markers present, plus deny-list category/redaction cases, bounds, hostile getters, unsupported platforms/mechanisms, envelope reconstruction, transport wrapping and the shipping optionsForDiagnostics path (with @sentry/react-native mocked to throw if loaded). A follow-up commit rewrote the vendor-prefix alternation as `[prs]k_(?:live|test)_` because the pre-existing bundle-secrets guard (__tests__/wf/be-mobile-security-secrets.test.ts) scans shipped source for the literal /sk_live/ — the guard was not modified. Full mobile jest on HEAD: 5916 passed, 1 pre-existing skipped, exit 0. No PR opened; only devin/pp/w10-01/impl-r1 pushed (4 commits on top of BASE_SHA, no force-push).
